name: Couchbase Server
model: JSON documents in buckets, scopes and collections, read by key or with SQL++ (SQL for JSON); full-text, vector and analytics services
engine_note: Memory-first cache over disk; Magma (hybrid LSM tree plus log-structured value store, default since 8.0) or Couchstore (copy-on-write B+tree)
consistency: Single-document writes atomic; multi-document ACID transactions optional (read committed). By default a write is acknowledged once in the active node's memory and replicated asynchronously, so it can be lost on failover; durability levels (majority, persist) are options.
scaling: Automatic sharding: each bucket is hashed into vBuckets spread over nodes, rebalanced when you add nodes; services (data, query, index, search) scale separately.
licence: Business Source License 1.1 (Couchbase Server 8.0; converts to Apache 2.0 on 2029-03-01)

licence_events.event: Couchbase announces Couchbase Server 7.0 source moves from Apache 2.0 to BSL 1.1 (source-available; each version converts to Apache 2.0 after its change date)
Haveli Investments completes its acquisition of Couchbase; the company goes private (not a licence change)

version_note: Release notes give month only (September 2026). 8.0 GA October 2025 made Magma the default storage engine.
reach: Reach for it when you want a JSON document store with a built-in memory cache, key lookups in about a millisecond, SQL-style queries, and mobile offline sync.
avoid: Avoid when you need strong multi-document guarantees by default, a small simple deployment, or an OSI open source licence.
escape: You want cache-speed key lookups and JSON queries in one cluster instead of Postgres plus Redis.
chat: User profiles and recent chats served at cache speed, with sync to a mobile client; most apps would not need it.
notes: couchbase.com blog and press pages returned HTTP 403 to this network, so the BSL announcement is dated from Couchbase's own SEC 10-Q ('In March 2021, we announced...'; exact day unconfirmed); the BSL file was added to kv_engine on 2021-04-13 and updated for 8.0 on 2025-01-09 with Change Date 2029-03-01. Transactions isolation per docs: read committed, with transactional reads at monotonic atomic view. Couchbase was acquired by Haveli Investments (announced 2025-06-20, closed 2025-09-24, about $1.5B) and is now private. Magma design per the VLDB 2022 paper (Lakshman et al.): 'a hybrid key-value storage engine that combines LSM Trees and a segmented log'; it contrasts with Couchstore's copy-on-write B+tree. Docs say the Magma 128-vBucket configuration is the default for new buckets from Enterprise 8.0. No Jepsen report.
